projects.name: QUD parsing
projects.label: Discourse structure
projects.note: A parser connects each sentence to an earlier sentence through the implicit question it answers.

projects.name: QUDeval
projects.label: Evaluating the questions
projects.note: Four linguistic criteria test whether a generated question fits its anchor, answer, and preceding text.

projects.name: QUDsim
projects.label: Comparing texts
projects.note: The questions answered by two documents reveal similarities in how they develop their ideas.

projects.name: ElabQUD
projects.label: Explaining added details
projects.note: Implicit questions describe the explanations editors add when simplifying an article.

projects.name: QSalience
projects.label: Which questions matter?
projects.note: We predict how much answering a question would help a reader understand the preceding text.

projects.name: MQUD
projects.label: Questions from figures
projects.note: Scientific figures raise questions about a paper’s argument. MQUD studies those questions with annotations from the papers’ authors.

projects.name: Bilingual disfluencies
projects.label: Predictability in speech
projects.note: Language model surprisal and linguistic features help us study disfluencies in monolingual and bilingual speech.

projects.name: ContextWeaver
projects.label: Memory for agents
projects.note: Dependencies between an agent’s reasoning steps guide which observations and decisions to retain in context.

connections.label: Evaluating QUD parsing
connections.description: QUDeval develops a human evaluation protocol for QUD parsing and examines the questions produced by parsing systems.

connections.label: QUD generation for text comparison
connections.description: QUDsim cites QUDeval in its question generation procedure, then uses answerability across documents to measure discourse similarity.

connections.label: From discourse structure to reader salience
connections.description: QUD parsing recovers the questions a text answers. QSalience asks which questions would most help a reader understand that text.

connections.label: Question validity
connections.description: QSalience follows QUDeval’s constraint that a question must be grounded in its anchor sentence when judging question validity.

connections.label: Choosing what to explain
connections.description: QSalience cites ElabQUD to motivate choosing which concepts need an explanation, beyond generating possible elaborations.

connections.label: From reader salience to scientific utility
connections.description: MQUD draws on QSalience when extending question salience from news text to scientific figures and a paper’s research goals.
